summary: Automated routing (auto-route) validation and safe rollback runbook for SLA rule rotations
description: Issue summary: We need a repeatable validation checklist and automated safety rollback for the support-tooling autoroute feature that rotates active SLA/routing rules. Impact: Recent config rotations caused two P0 customer routings to mis-classify support requests (route->internal queue) for ~12 minutes each. While no customer data was lost, alerts were suppressed and response SLAs were missed. Background: The autoroute pipeline rotates sets of routing macros nightly; rotations apply new priority mappings and SLA rule IDs. There is an existing manual rollback but no validated gating tests or automated rollback trigger. Goal: Create a validation pipeline (pre-traffic checks + post-apply assertions), documentation runbook, and an automated rollback signal tied to the reporting pipeline. Deliverables: 1) Pre-deploy test suite (synthetic tickets + assertions), 2) Post-deploy sanity checks (route metrics, SLA assignment counts, error rate deltas), 3) Automated rollback play that triggers on threshold breaches, 4) Update to runbook and on-call checklist.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Nightly autoroute job applies rule set RS-2026-03 to routing-service.
2) New priority mapping accidentally omits enterprise-tier tag causing those tickets to map to internal-support queue.
3) Monitoring alerts not triggered because rule-assignment metric name changed in rule set.
4) Rollback deferred until manual detection via CS reports.
observed_behavior: Enterprise-tier tickets routed to internal queue; SLA-assignment metric dropped 80% for component 'support.priority.assign' for ~12 minutes on 2026-03-08 and 2026-03-09.
expected_behavior: Autoroute rotations should be gated by automated tests and post-apply assertions; on threshold breach the pipeline should auto-rollback to the last known-good rule set and page SRE + Support Ops.
temporary_workaround: Manually re-applied previous rule set RS-2026-02 via support-tooling console and incremented a temporary feature-flag to disable nightly rotations. Manual checks performed on routing counts.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-08: Initial incident logged by CS after receiving multiple customer Slack reports (#support-enterprise).

SRE review: change in rule set removed expected 'enterprise_tier' label in two rule clauses; metrics pipeline was using the older metric name 'support.priority.assign' and new rule set emitted 'support.priority.assignment' causing the alerting query to return 0s.
Support-tooling job logs (deploy job 4573) show successful apply with no schema validation errors because schema check validates syntax, not semantics (missing label).
Hypothesis: lack of semantic validation for required tags + reliance on exact metric names caused silent failure of detection.
proposed_next_steps:
1) Implement a pre-apply synthetic test harness that creates synthetic tickets for each tier and asserts expected route and SLA assignment.
2) Add a small post-apply validator that queries both metric name variants for a 2-minute window and compares assignment counts to a baseline.
3) Add a configurable rollback trigger: if assignment delta > 20% for any tier for 2 consecutive minutes, auto-rollback and open INT ticket and page SRE + Support Ops.
4) Update runbook with step-by-step rollback commands, Slack escalation template, and checklist for validating fixes.
5) Create a small daily report that surfaces rule-rotation diffs and top 5 affected routes for the last 24h.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Samir Kapoor (SRE): Confirmed metric name mismatch; raising a patch to monitoring to read both names for 48h to avoid blind spots.
2026-03-11 - Emily Chen (Support Ops): Adding request to include 'enterprise_tier' presence as a gate in CI for rule sets. Will draft macro template for synthetic tickets.
2026-03-12 - Marco Ruiz (Platform Eng): I can add the pre-apply harness; need list of canonical tiers and a sandbox routing service to run tests against.
resolution: In progress - design agreed. Implementation tickets split: pre-apply harness, post-apply validator, rollback automation. ETA for delivery: 2026-03-28
